A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LPD research, with matching authors, core method, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, efficiency measurements, attention analyses, and ablations, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 7 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds text-to-image evaluation, threshold sensitivity experiments, and throughput measurements across batch sizes.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a text-conditioning adaptation: Gemma-2-2B embeddings pass through a linear projection and precede image embeddings, replacing class-label conditioning for text-to-image generation. The original attention masks, decoding procedure, and locality-ordering implementation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet class-conditioned generation and zero-shot editing. v2 additionally trains on approximately 10 million internal synthetic images with captions and evaluates 1024×1024 text-to-image generation on GenEval, substantially expanding the represented data and conditioning task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and Figure 9 is unchanged. The added text-to-image and throughput experiments reuse the raster-order counterpart as their control. The expanded discussion of ZipAR does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The added text-to-image experiments introduce GenEval evaluation and a three-stage training schedule: 40, 5, and 2 epochs at 256, 512, and 1024 resolution, with specified model-dependent batch sizes. New protocols also sweep ordering thresholds and increase inference batch size until memory exhaustion. These are additions, not evidence that the retained ImageNet experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 6 add sensitivity tests of both ordering thresholds. Section 3.3 and Appendix E add throughput scaling across batch sizes and three model sizes, testing where acceleration diminishes. These substantially extend analysis of parameter sensitivity and practical efficiency; the original Figure 9 ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain latency averaging over 500 inference steps after 100 warm-up steps. The added experiments continue to report point estimates without new uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain numerically unchanged. New Table 3 reports GenEval scores of 0.58/0.62 for LPD-L/XL versus 0.55/0.60 for their raster counterparts, using 64 versus 4096 steps. Table 7 adds category scores, Table 6 adds threshold-dependent FIDs, and Figure 14 adds throughput curves. These are newly reported results, not improvements over corresponding v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorizations, Per-Token Attention definition, and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Cardinality notation is clarified, but no substantive definition, theorem, proof, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two contributions and headline claims: flexible parallelized modeling, locality-aware ordering, reduced ImageNet generation steps, and at least 3.4× lower latency. The added experiments do not revise these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains that query tokens increase computation, making speedups smaller as inference becomes compute-bound at larger batches. Appendix B.3 adds explanations of threshold tradeoffs, and Section 3.2 interprets the text-to-image results as evidence of broader applicability. These extend the interpretation without replacing the original locality explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds substantial implementation information: the text encoder and projection, Qwen2.5-VL-32B recaptioning, caption sampling, and staged training budgets. The existing ordering code is merely relocated. Reproducibility remains qualified: the new data are internal, and Appendix B.3 reverses Algorithm 1's threshold symbols and states defaults inconsistent with the retained code.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GenEval, Gemma 2, and Qwen2.5-VL. It expands the comparison with PAR, NAR, and ZipAR, acknowledging their mutual visibility, and adds Appendix B.2's claim that LPD uniquely quantifies and jointly optimizes both locality principles. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized prose and caption revisions. Zero-shot editing moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix D, efficiency analysis takes its place, and the appendices are reorganized. Some new editing errors appear in Section 3.1, including 'reportuse' and '50k,000'.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual evidence through GenEval Tables 3 and 7, sensitivity Table 6, a text-to-image gallery in Figure 13, and throughput plots in Figure 14. The original generation gallery moves from Figure 10 in the main text to Figure 12 in Appendix D. Existing attention visualizations are retained and renumbered; Figure 7's axis label is clarified.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence beyond class-conditioned ImageNet generation and explains when acceleration weakens at larger batches. Sensitivity tests and the text-to-image training recipe improve assessability. These gains are tempered by the internal training dataset, inconsistent threshold notation/defaults, and new editing errors. The result is a limited net improvement to an otherwise largely retained scientific core.
